raw_case_text:
A 60-year-old Lebanese man was referred to the pulmonology clinic in January 2023 for evaluation of an incidental pulmonary nodule identified during a cardiac CT angiogram. He worked in the IT department and was a current occasional smoker (< 5 pack years). His medical history included cervical disc prolapse, a benign thyroid nodule, pre-diabetes, and moderate obstructive sleep apnoea. His regular medications included ezetimibe, clopidogrel, esomeprazole, alfuzosin, and rosuvastatin.
The cardiac CT angiogram was performed to evaluate mild exertional dyspnoea, which the patient experienced for over a year following an acute cervical disc prolapse that resulted in reduced mobility. Symptoms gradually resolved over several months. Pulmonary function tests, a six-minute walk test, and cardiology evaluation (echocardiography and stress test) showed no abnormalities. The mild exertional dyspnoea, which resolved spontaneously, was attributed to deconditioning after the cervical disc prolapse. The patient intentionally lost weight (9 kg) due to a recent diagnosis of pre-diabetes. The patient did not report fever or night sweats.
Laboratory Data:
Normal CD4 count (650 cells/microL), IgE (45 IU/mL), CRP (2 mg/L).
Negative Echinococcus serology (ELISA), normal eosinophils (2 %).
Lung Function Tests:
FEV1: 92 % predicted, FVC: 95 % predicted, DLCO: 88 % predicted.
Physical examination revealed a respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, blood pressure of 129/74 mmHg, heart rate of 66 bpm, temperature of 36.2  C, and oxygen saturation of 99 % on room air. His height was 175 cm, weight 77 kg, and BMI 25.14. There was nothing significant on respiratory examination.
A cardiac CT angiogram in January 2023 detected a 3 mm pulmonary nodule in the left lingula. A high-resolution chest CT in January 2024 identified two nodules: an 8.5 mm calcified nodule in the left upper lobe and a 9.4 x 5 mm nodule in the right upper lobe, along with an incidental 7 x 4 mm well-defined, pleural-based fusiform cystic lesion. A follow-up chest CT in September 2024 showed no growth in the pulmonary nodules, both deemed benign. However, the pleural-based lesion had enlarged significantly (from 7 x 4 mm to 3.1 x 1.7 cm) with adjacent rib erosion. A thoracic MRI confirmed a well-defined fusiform pleural lesion at the right 4th rib level, causing bony erosion (Fig. 1). Differential diagnoses included primary pleural liposarcoma or aggressive solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura.
The case was discussed in the lung cancer multidisciplinary team meeting. A CT-guided biopsy in October 2024 confirmed a hydatid cyst with no malignant features (Fig. 4). Liver involvement was excluded on MRI, and the cyst appeared isolated to the pleura. Laboratory tests, including white cell count, eosinophil count, IgE, CRP, and serology for Schistosoma and Echinococcus, were normal or negative.
The patient initiated albendazole 400 mg twice daily for three months. At a four-week follow-up in November 2024, he described a two-week history of intermittent, mild-to-moderate, well-localized, right-sided pleuritic chest pain. No fever, dyspnoea, or weight loss was reported. A repeat thoracic MRI on December 2, 2024, revealed significant regression of the pleural hydatid cyst, with the lesion size decreasing from 12 x 10 mm to 7 x 4 mm and resolution of surrounding inflammation (Fig. 2).
The chest pain subsided within a few weeks. The patient was reassured, and albendazole therapy continued for a total duration of five months. A final MRI, conducted three months after stopping albendazole, confirmed complete resolution of the pleural hydatid cyst (Fig. 3).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 60-year-old Lebanese man was referred for evaluation of an incidental pulmonary nodule and subsequently developed an enlarging right pleural cystic lesion.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was referred to the pulmonology clinic in January 2023 after a cardiac CT angiogram (performed for a >1-year history of mild exertional dyspnea that resolved spontaneously following deconditioning from an acute cervical disc prolapse) identified a 3-mm left lingular nodule. He had intentionally lost 9 kg following a diagnosis of pre-diabetes. Serial chest CTs in January and September 2024 revealed an enlarging right pleural-based cystic lesion.
subjective.past_medical_history: Cervical disc prolapse, benign thyroid nodule, pre-diabetes, and moderate obstructive sleep apnea. Worked in an IT department and was an occasional smoker (<5 pack-years).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for resolved mild exertional dyspnea and intentional 9-kg weight loss; negative for fever or night sweats. Home medications: ezetimibe, clopidogrel, esomeprazole, alfuzosin, and rosuvastatin.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, blood pressure 129/74 mmHg, heart rate 66 bpm, temperature 36.2 C, SpO2 99% on room air, height 175 cm, weight 77 kg, BMI 25.14 kg/m2. Respiratory and systemic examinations were unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed normal WBC, normal eosinophils (2%), normal CD4 count (650 cells/uL), IgE 45 IU/mL, CRP 2 mg/L, and negative Echinococcus and Schistosoma ELISA serologies. Pulmonary function tests were normal (FEV1 92% predicted, FVC 95% predicted, DLCO 88% predicted), as were 6-minute walk test, echocardiography, and cardiac stress test.
objective.advanced_workup: Cardiac CT angiogram (Jan 2023) showed a 3-mm left lingular nodule. HRCT chest (Jan 2024) identified an 8.5-mm calcified left upper lobe nodule, a 9.4 x 5 mm right upper lobe nodule, and an incidental 7 x 4 mm right pleural-based fusiform cystic lesion, which enlarged to 3.1 x 1.7 cm with adjacent right 4th rib erosion on follow-up chest CT (Sep 2024) and thoracic MRI (abdominal MRI excluded liver involvement). CT-guided pleural biopsy in October 2024 confirmed a hydatid cyst without malignancy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Primary isolated right pleural hydatid cyst with 4th rib erosion, confirmed by CT-guided biopsy histopathology despite negative Echinococcus ELISA serology (ruling out primary pleural liposarcoma and aggressive solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura). The patient was treated medically with oral albendazole 400 mg twice daily for a total of 5 months; transient right pleuritic chest pain at 4 weeks coincided with cyst regression on December 2024 MRI (from 12 x 10 mm to 7 x 4 mm), and a final thoracic MRI 3 months after completing albendazole confirmed complete resolution.
